name: Auditory cortical pitch representation
summary: A cortical neural representation of perceptual pitch that can integrate different acoustic cues. It is modeled as neural activity carrying pitch information, not as a hidden oscillator whose carrier must equal the sound's fundamental frequency.

axis.notes: Temporal spectrum of cortical neural activity; pitch information is encoded in the response, but no carrier-frequency identity with the acoustic stimulus is asserted.

constraints: pitch representations can generalize across acoustic cue types
fundamental frequency, harmonic spacing, and context can all contribute to pitch
the neural representation is not assumed to oscillate at the perceived pitch frequency

relationships.description: Auditory-nerve activity carries cochlear information toward the brain, where cortical responses encode pitch-relevant information.
A shared cortical representation of pitch contributes to the stable pitch percept elicited by different acoustic cues; the precise neural mechanism remains an active research question.

sources.title: How Do We Hear?
sources.publisher: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders (NIDCD), NIH

sources.title: Dynamics of Pitch Perception in the Auditory Cortex

evidence.derivation: The study decodes pitch from cortical neural responses across multiple acoustic cue types. Atlas therefore represents pitch as encoded neural information while leaving the neural signal's own temporal spectrum unresolved.
